newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli troops, Palestinians clash in Bethlehem.
newsitem.headline: Israeli troops, Palestinians clash in Bethlehem.

text.p: Israeli troops fired rubber bullets at Palestinians who hurled stones in the West Bank town of Bethlehem on Friday after a rally in memory of a man who died in Israeli custody, witnesses said.
They said two Palestinians were wounded by a rubber bullets.

The clashes erupted when some 500 Palestinians at a rally in memory of Khaled Abu Daiyeh, a Palestinian whose family said Israeli authorities tortured him to death in custody, began to march toward Rachel's Tomb Jewish shrine on the outskirts of Bethlehem, which is guarded by Israeli troops.
Most of Bethlehem is under Palestinian rule.
Witnesses said Palestinian police formed a human barrier to prevent demonstrators reaching the Israelis, but they were not able to hold back the crowd.
Abu Daiyeh's body was handed to his family in Bethlehem by Israel last week.
A Reuters cameraman who filmed the body said the skull was crushed, the chest caved in, and the hands and legs appeared broken.
The Palestinian Authority's chief pathologist, who examined Abu Daiyeh's body before burial, ruled he died of "neurological shock caused by severe pain resulting from external violence".

Israeli police said Abu Daiyeh, arrested for trying to take a policeman's gun in Jerusalem's Old City, felt unwell and was taken to Jerusalem's Shaare Zedek hospital. At the hospital, Abu Daiyeh refused treatment and "went crazy", attacking anyone who came near him, police said.
He was brought under control and put to bed, they said. He was found dead in his bed on Wednesday, they said, adding that the Justice Ministry was investigating.
Israel's Haaretz newspaper said last Friday that guards at the hospital may have fatally beaten Abu Daiyeh.

Hospital head Yonatan Halevy told Israel Radio hospital guards "were not the dominant or meaningful element in this violence...The violence used, justly or unjustly, to prevent danger to the public, was used by police."
